dimension_justifications.soundness: The manuscript is admirably explicit about its boundaries, but every empirical result is source-reported and the snapshot lacks the records needed to verify the treatment, score construction, samples, estimates, or intervals. Thus the central empirical claims remain cannot_verify rather than demonstrated findings.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is concise, anonymous, logically sectioned, and unusually careful about descriptive versus causal language, the recorded-single-decode estimand, differing samples, Brier/NLL semantics, and MATH500 scenario status. Presentation nevertheless suffers from an unresolved paper identity, undefined treatment and score terminology, an operationally undefined notion of comparable magnitude, opaque revision/audit language, and table precision inconsistencies.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The strongest contribution is a careful formal and linguistic boundary around an existing source-reported comparison. Because no result is independently supported, the central comparison has no decision rule, and the literature search is explicitly incomplete, the snapshot does not yet establish substantial new knowledge or capability.

paper_summary: The paper juxtaposes a source-reported observational natural-length contrast on GSM8K (+0.2227) with a source-reported 400-item paired fixed-filler contrast under NFE=64 (-0.0075, reported bracket [-0.052,+0.039]). It formalizes the latter as a finite-pool contrast conditional on one recorded decode realization, not an expectation over items or decoder randomness. It further reports Brier- and NLL-labelled numerical diagnostics and an ancillary MATH500 judge-convention scenario while explicitly denying causal, answer-calibration, replication, and cross-benchmark interpretations. The manuscript is principally an evidence-boundary and transcription document because the frozen package contains none of the underlying experimental records or implementations.
strongest_verified_contribution: The clearest verified contribution is the formal distinction in Sections 2-3 between a finite-pool recorded-realization estimand and a decoder- or population-expectation estimand, together with consistent warnings that the natural-strata and paired-filler estimates have different samples and targets. The displayed +0.2227 natural-strata decomposition is also arithmetically correct, although its inputs remain source-reported.
strengths: Sections 2-3 define the recorded-single-decode estimand clearly and explicitly exclude generalization over decoder randomness, prompts, fillers, and problem populations.

The abstract, Sections 1 and 4.2, and the conclusion consistently describe the natural-versus-filler comparison as descriptive and avoid a causal or inferential comparison between the two reported estimates.
The paper responsibly avoids calling the commit score an answer probability and treats the Brier/NLL values as labelled numerical diagnostics rather than validated answer-level calibration measures.
Section 5 correctly labels the purposive-anchor MATH500 band as a scenario range rather than a confidence interval and disclaims replication or cross-benchmark confirmation.
The manuscript is concise, uses a clear evidence hierarchy, remains anonymous, contains an AI-assistance disclosure, and fits comfortably within the nine-page main-text limit.
questions: What exactly is the item-level commit score s: which token commitments enter it, how are they aggregated, what is its range, and what answer-level forecast event—if any—does it represent?

What were the literal filler string, insertion location, tokenizer and tokenization result, 400-item selection rule, prompt serialization, arm order, model/tokenizer revision, matcher, and decoding configuration?
What pre-specified quantitative rule or margin would make a filler effect comparably large relative to the natural-strata estimate, given the different samples and estimands?
What quantity do the MATH500 values +0.2382 and +0.1606 represent, and how are the answer-aware convention, lenient convention, purposive anchors, and adjustment computed?
Are the arm means in Table 3 rounded from hidden-precision values? If so, can sufficient digits or an explicit rounding note be supplied so the displayed contrasts reproduce exactly?

issues.location: PDF p. 2, Section 2, paragraph 'What is missing'; pp. 3-4, Sections 4-7 and Tables 2-3; reviewer-safe experiment registry A32-X1-A32-X3
issues.observed_evidence: This is a cannot_verify condition, not a demonstrated numerical error. The snapshot contains no item-level records, manifests, literal filler, prompt serialization, tokenizer dose fixture, decode traces, score construction, judge outputs, interval code, model revision, or executable analysis. The evidence IDs are explicitly described as opaque references to missing records.
issues.why_it_matters: Every empirical claim and the paper's operation-specific contribution depend on these absent materials. Honest caveats prevent overclaiming but do not convert unverifiable source reports into conference-grade evidence.
issues.required_fix: Provide an immutable, anonymous experimental bundle containing the exact samples and exclusions, literal prompts and filler insertion, tokenizer and +37-token verification, model/tokenizer revisions, decode configuration and randomness controls, per-item arm outputs and labels, score traces, judge/anchor records, and code that regenerates every table and interval.
issues.verification_test: From a clean environment, resolve every evidence ID to a file, reconstruct both samples and the paired arms, confirm the filler adds exactly 37 tokenizer tokens at the stated location under NFE=64, recompute all arm summaries and intervals, and reproduce Tables 2-3 and the MATH500 scenario within stated numerical tolerance.
issues.evidence_needed: Reviewer-safe raw or losslessly derived records, immutable manifests, prompts, configurations, environment lock, score and matcher implementations, bootstrap seeds/replicates, analysis scripts, and a claim-to-file crosswalk.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Section 1; p. 2, Section 2; p. 3, Section 4.2, paragraphs following Table 3; p. 5, Conclusion
issues.observed_evidence: The central question asks whether the filler change is 'comparable in magnitude' to +0.2227, but the paper supplies no equivalence or separation margin, joint estimand, common sample, covariance estimate, or pre-specified comparison rule. It correctly acknowledges this gap and ultimately compares only absolute point estimates from different samples and estimands.
issues.why_it_matters: Without an operational criterion, the headline diagnostic cannot answer its stated question; it produces a visual juxtaposition rather than a falsifiable conclusion about comparability.
issues.required_fix: Either redefine the contribution strictly as a descriptive juxtaposition and remove language claiming to diagnose whether the effect is comparably large, or specify a scientifically justified margin and evaluate an aligned common-sample or otherwise valid joint contrast with uncertainty.
issues.verification_test: Before examining results, state a numerical comparison rule and its estimand; then show that a common-sample or justified joint analysis produces an interval that supports one of the pre-specified outcomes. A blind reader should be able to decide the result mechanically from that rule.
issues.evidence_needed: Aligned item identities and outcomes, overlap information, item-level paired data, covariance-aware uncertainty, and a justified pre-specified comparison margin.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Section 1, paragraphs defining the cross-level quantity; p. 2, Section 3, equations for D and Delta; p. 3, Table 3 and 'Score-based loss diagnostics'; p. 4, Section 7
issues.observed_evidence: The paper denotes an item-level s as a 'source-recorded commit score' but never defines how token-level commitment measurements become that scalar, which tokens are included, its scale, or its forecast event. The omission is acknowledged. Consequently, even the meaning of subtracting s from binary final-answer correctness and applying Brier/NLL-labelled transformations cannot be independently assessed.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's principal outcome is arithmetically defined but lacks enough construct definition for interpretation, reproduction, or comparison across arms. Careful renaming avoids a false calibration claim but does not supply measurement validity.
issues.required_fix: Define the commit-score extraction and aggregation algorithm formally, state its range and timing, identify the corresponding outcome event, explain why the cross-level subtraction is informative, and provide construct-validation or sensitivity evidence. If no answer-probability interpretation is intended, motivate precisely what decision-relevant property the diagnostic measures.
issues.verification_test: Given released token-level traces, an independent implementation should reproduce every item-level s and all aggregate diagnostics. Construct checks should show how the measure behaves under known correct/incorrect answers and under alternative aggregation rules.
issues.evidence_needed: Token-level commitment traces, exact aggregation code, answer matcher, score range/event definition, validation fixtures, and robustness analyses over defensible aggregation choices.

issues.location: PDF pp. 1-4 throughout, especially p. 1 Abstract and 'Measurement status'; p. 3 'Omitted random-dose analysis'; p. 4 Sections 5 and 7
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript repeatedly refers to an unexplained 'source manuscript,' 'source-described record,' 'current package,' facts 'retained' from elsewhere, 'prior prose,' and the 'authoring directory inspected for this revision.' Opaque E1-E4 identifiers do not resolve to experimental files. This makes the paper read as an internal forensic revision memo rather than a self-contained account of a study or a clearly framed reproducibility audit.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader cannot cleanly determine which scientific work the authors performed, which work they merely transcribed, or what paper genre and contribution are being submitted. The process-history language also dilutes a very short manuscript.
issues.required_fix: Choose and state a coherent paper identity. For an empirical study, describe methods and results directly and attach their evidence. For a reproducibility or evidence audit, identify the audited object and protocol and make the audit itself systematic and reproducible. Remove revision-history language, and map every evidence identifier to an accessible artifact.
issues.verification_test: Give the revised manuscript and artifact index to a blind reader; the reader should be able to state unambiguously what the authors did, what was inherited, what was verified, and where each supporting record resides without access to revision history.
issues.evidence_needed: A self-contained methods/provenance account, stable evidence crosswalk, and accessible records supporting whichever paper identity is selected.

issues.location: PDF p. 4, Section 6, especially the final sentence; citation_lock.json field 'remaining_unverified_scope'
issues.observed_evidence: The related-work section covers three neighboring prompt-calibration studies but explicitly states that a broader prompt-length-specific and masked-diffusion uncertainty search is incomplete. The included citation lock supports only the stated narrow boundaries and likewise identifies the remaining search gap.
issues.why_it_matters: The claimed operation-specific contribution cannot be confidently distinguished from existing prompt-length, filler, inference-compute, or masked-diffusion uncertainty studies under the current literature evidence.
issues.required_fix: Complete and document a broader primary-source search, then compare the proposed estimand, intervention, model family, fixed-compute condition, and score construction against the closest work in a compact taxonomy.
issues.verification_test: A reproducible literature search and claim matrix should identify the nearest prompt-length/filler and masked-diffusion uncertainty studies and show, claim by claim, which element of the present contribution is absent from each.
issues.evidence_needed: Search protocol and date, queried databases and terms, screened primary sources, exclusion rationale, and an updated comparison table.

issues.observed_evidence: Displayed precision is inconsistent. For example, the commit-score arm means 0.630 and 0.543 imply -0.087 at shown precision, while the table reports -0.0875. Likewise, the displayed arm means imply cross-level differences of about -0.073 and -0.080 rather than the four-decimal values -0.0724 and -0.0799. Hidden-precision rounding is plausible, but the table does not say so.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper emphasizes transcription arithmetic and auditability, so readers should be able to reconcile displayed components and contrasts without guessing about hidden digits.
issues.required_fix: Use consistent sufficient precision for arm means and contrasts, or add a note stating that contrasts were computed before rounding. Ideally include counts or standard errors where applicable and apply one precision convention across Tables 2-3.
issues.verification_test: Recompute every displayed difference from the displayed arm values; each should match exactly at the declared rounding tolerance.
issues.evidence_needed: Unrounded aggregate values and a documented table-rounding rule.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, contribution item 3 ('cross-bed confirmation'); p. 4, Section 5 and Section 6 ('semantics-preserving length-only filler')
issues.observed_evidence: Several terms are undefined or cross-sectionally inconsistent. 'Cross-bed confirmation' is not explained and appears to mean cross-benchmark confirmation. Section 5 does not name the metric represented by its two convention values or define the conventions and anchor adjustment. Section 6 calls the filler 'semantics-preserving' even though Sections 2 and 4.2 state that the literal filler and insertion location are missing, so semantic preservation cannot be checked.
issues.why_it_matters: These terms obscure the ancillary scenario and over-specify an unverified treatment property, weakening an otherwise careful terminology policy.
issues.required_fix: Correct or define 'cross-bed,' explicitly name the MATH500 quantity and equations, define both judge conventions and the anchor adjustment, and remove 'semantics-preserving' unless treatment content and validation are supplied.
issues.verification_test: A terminology audit should give each central noun phrase one definition and consistent use. Independent readers should be able to identify the MATH500 estimand and reproduce its adjustment, while a released filler audit should substantiate any semantic-preservation claim.
issues.evidence_needed: Exact MATH500 formulas and judge protocol, anchor records, literal filler and insertion rule, and a documented semantic-invariance check if that descriptor is retained.

ethics_concerns: No specific human-subject, privacy, safety, or dual-use concern is evident from the frozen snapshot. The absence of experimental provenance is a scientific reproducibility problem rather than, on the available evidence, a distinct ethics violation.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. It was based only on the frozen reviewer snapshot and did not use the internet, repository history, prior reviews, author notes, or files outside the submission directory.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A complete reviewer-safe artifact bundle that independently reproduces all rows and intervals in Tables 2-3 and the MATH500 scenario.
A precise, validated definition of the item-level commit score and its relationship to the final-answer event, including robustness to alternative aggregation choices.
An aligned common-sample comparison or pre-specified comparability margin with joint uncertainty that converts the headline juxtaposition into a falsifiable diagnostic.
A coherent self-contained paper identity, stable claim-to-artifact mapping, and removal of revision-process language.
A completed primary-source literature audit establishing the operation-specific novelty boundary.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure to reproduce any reported point estimate or bracket from released item-level data and code.
Evidence that the filler is not exactly +37 tokens under the stated tokenizer, changes task semantics, or is inserted inconsistently across items.
Evidence that the 400-item sample or pairing differs from the manuscript description, contains undisclosed exclusions, or overlaps with the natural sample in a way that changes the comparison.
Repeated paired decodes showing that decoder-run variability dominates or reverses the recorded-single-realization contrast.
Evidence that the cited neighboring-work descriptions are inaccurate or that prior work already evaluates the same fixed-filler, fixed-NFE masked-diffusion estimand.
review_limitations: The review was restricted to the five-page PDF and reviewer-safe files in the frozen snapshot.
No underlying experimental records or executable analysis were available, so empirical correctness and interval coverage could not be independently checked.
Literature completeness could not be assessed beyond the included citation lock because external search was prohibited.
Visual assessment was based on the complete extracted PDF content and metadata; no editable LaTeX source was included in the reviewer snapshot.
